newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: More Asian cargo destinations eyed by KAL.
newsitem.headline: More Asian cargo destinations eyed by KAL.

text.p: New Asian cargo destinations are being considered by Korean Airlines cargo vice president and general manager, Ji Young Lee told Reuters in an interview.

A third weekly Airbus A300 freighter service to Shenzhen in Guangdong province is being studied, while talks are underway with Vietnam Airlines for cargo flights to Ho Chi Minh City and possibly Saigon, he said.
Dhaka in Bangladesh is another potential cargo destination, Lee added.
In China, KAL is frustrated at not being allowed cargo flights to supplement its passenger services to Beijing, Shanghai, Qingdao, Tianjin, Dalian, Shenyang and Sanya, Lee said.

But KAL is able to increasingly use sea/air freight using vessels from its parent Hanjin Shipping Co Ltd -- also part of the giant Hanjin Group -- to transport freight from Chinese ports to Pusan in southern Korea. This is then trucked to Seoul for distribution on KAL's worldwide air cargo network.
"It is a trend which is growing all the time and a way of expanding the market. The sea/air rate structure is very competitive," Lee said.
Last month KAL also launched a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter service to Sydney targetting the Australian perishables market. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
